title: The Univer-City
_galleryFieldsHelp: Set galleryOrder (number) to control homepage order and showInGallery (true/false) to include or hide.
description: The university is a meltingpot of different science, of different knowledge. It’s an alternative disciplin that indirectly support our society. The idea of universe-city aim to break the imagining frontier between those two entities, it makes of the university an open space, with multiple sources. In our vision of the territory, it make sense to see Brussel as a complex web, where the universe-cities has an important role. The pole solbosh play his part in it. We highlighted 5 main aspects of the Solbosch campus and its surrounding at the scale of the Brussels University District. Linking the campus to the city, mobility systems , the landscape design, the environmental developments (including water management, and energy) and the notion of harmonism, in broad aspects, are the main point of concerns. These strategies not only help us to discuss sustainability beyond the environmental issues, but the social and economical levels are also taken into account. Through connecting the university with the city of Brussel, the campus will be transformed into open space for the neighborhood. Our first ambition is to open the campus to the city. Regarding this, we provide several common areas such as swimming, sport fields, urban farming, a rooftop playground, open libraries, a café and food services, a ressourcery, auditoriums and finally multi-functional areas to be shared for public events, conferences, etc. Therefore the new entrance building will be filled with community services as a link to the city. We then focus on the mobility on the scale of the campus and the BUD.
client: Yasmin Allaouzi, Niloofar Amini, Paulien Beeckman, Pauline Harou, Ahmed Soliman, and Alexandre Rovere

title: Leap of Faith Bridge
description: We got the second place in FEDA week 13 students’ National competition 2012/13 in the topic of (Bridge of the Future), competing with more than 60 other university, our project was designed to provide responsive moves that varies with the different conditions. The bridge represent the leap of faith people should take to pass from their past to the future. With a middle glass part to form an obstacle that will face people in their life, Users have to choose to step forward and take the leap to the future.
client: Mohamed Mahmoud, Mazen Nabil, Fatma Abd Elrahman, Abdullah gabr, Ayman Shawki, Mostfafa Elsayed, Haytham Kamal , Ahmed Soliman.

title: Bending-active responsive grid shell
description:
The project is an attempt to combine bending-active structural elements in a responsive system. The pavilion consists of a grid-shell that can be controlled with set of wires. The wires can be separately tensioned by the users according to different needs and weather. The aims of the project is to enrich the connection between Brussels locals and the outdoor spaces. Giving the opportunity to the users to alter and shape the pavilion. The seven tensioned wires of the pavilion shape tens of alternatives. 

 Temporary structures are everywhere. They define the outdoor spaces and fill the void between permanent constructions. They follow the organic evolution of cities’ needs and daily functions. Such organic development should be backed by transformable systems that provide flexibility. Transformable structure systems change from one state to another. They can be rapidly assembled and disassembled, then transported to another place to reuse the same materials and reduce the amount of waste.
role: Design, Research, structural analysis, parametric modeling

title: The Chavilion: Scissor chair-pavilion
description:
The Chavilion is a design project to create an indoor pavilion for the architectural atelier at VUB. The pavilion is a kit of parts system consists of a main repetitive unit. The system is intended to work as a Lego to assure transformability. The main block in the system is a stand-alone functional chair with scissor deplorability. Fixing 6-8 chairs together creates the arch of the pavilion that is still deployable. 

 The project included a structural analysis using “Karamba3D” plugin on grasshopper, it also included creating a 1/5 scaled scissor system to test the whole project functionality. The chair utilized the scissor system to provide 5 different shapes of uses.
role: Conceptualization, Design, Research, structural analysis, parametric modeling
client: Ahmed Soliman, Hana Taherazar, Pauline Harou, Razan Atwi.

title: ULB timber tower: timber is the new concrete
description: The ULB Timber Tower is part of a master plan to develop the ULB campus in Brussels, Belgium. The project proposes an entrance building that directly welcomes visitors and students arriving along the campus's main axis. The aims of the ULB Timber Tower reflect the vision of the master plan while pursuing four main goals: 1) to promote sustainability and lead the community by example; 2) to establish a symbolic identity for the university; 3) to strengthen the connection between the city and the university; and 4) to provide the functional spaces needed to accommodate the constant increase in students and expand university capacity.
role: Conceptualization, Design, Research, structural analysis, enviromental analysis, parametric modeling, Night shots post-production by Mohamed Mahmoud

title: Konligo: Internship - Research and development
description: Konligo is a Belgian start-up specialized in lightweight and transformable structures. Its main mission is to push temporary structures to the next level, while pushing the event industry to a more sustainable future. I joined the R&D team and participated in developing the deployable scissor structure technology. During my internship in Konligo, I had the chance to work in several departments. One of the perks of working in relatively small teams is to get involved in a lot of different fields and get a broader experience of how everything works. I was trained as an engineer, but I also learned a lot of entrepreneur’s skills.
role: R&D, Research, parametric modeling, computational production, Graphic design, video editing, The Structure is originally designed by konligo team.

title: Prison de Saint-Gilles: 2030
description:
The prisons of Saint-Gilles have been emptied, leaving an exceptional land area of more than 10ha to be rehabilitated close to the center of Brussels. We developed a full plan for turning the prison’s building into a multi-functional project that liberate the land and give the plot back to the city. The project won the first place in “Design project competition” course. Taught by Vincent Gérin and judged by jury members: Luc Deleuze, Laurent Vrijdaghs, Vincent Wathelet, John Pitseys, Françoise Sacchi. 

 I had the opportunity to share the stage of the “realty Belgium’s real estate summit” with Benoit Moritz, Laurent Vrijdaghs, and Vincent Gérin as part of discussing case studies of the reconversion of the Saint Gilles Prison September, 2022.
role: Design, Research, Financial plans, conceptualization, computational production, rendering.

title: Bending-active plate components in configurable kit-of-pats systems
description: This research investigates transformable wooden kit-of-parts systems through digital and physical modeling. It conceptualizes the structure as an assembly of modular components constructed on site and proposes a reconfigurable temporary system capable of adapting to different shapes and sizes using a consistent set of elements. A systematic method for connecting components is introduced, based on joints arranged within symmetrical grids and solids. Each face is replaced by a modular element, with pairs of elements connected through a single joint. The resulting structural configurations are derived from thoroughly studied polyhedral geometries or tessellations. The regularity of these systems is key to their reconfigurability.

title: First permanent moon base
description:
The spacefaring age promises immense potential, offering humanity access to vast resources, materials, and energy beyond Earth. In 2004, George W. Bush introduced a vision for renewed lunar exploration through a series of robotic missions designed to gather data on lunar resources and identify suitable construction sites for future habitation.

This project presents a vision, conceived in 2014, of an early step toward the colonization of the Moon. It explores the development of an initial unmanned lunar base as the foundation for a permanent human presence.

The first permanent Moon base represents a critical milestone in the transition to a new era of exploration. It will enable deeper access to the solar system, support the establishment of extraterrestrial settlements, and shift humanity’s perspective from a “closed Earth” mindset to a broader, open-space vision of progress and discovery.

title: The Barber
description:
An interior design project for “The Barbershop,” a growing chain of barbershops based in Egypt. Designed and implemented in 2020, the project was developed by Soliman in collaboration with co-designer Aaacer El Noshokaty, working as freelance architects.

The project encompassed the full interior design process, from concept development to detailed execution drawings, with a focus on creating a distinctive and contemporary spatial identity. The design aimed to reinterpret the traditional barbershop experience through a modern lens, balancing functionality, comfort, and a strong visual character.

In parallel, the scope included the development of a complete brand identity, covering logo design, visual language, and overall branding strategy to ensure coherence between the physical space and the brand’s image.

The shop is currently operational in Cairo.
role: Interior design, rendering, modeling, lighting, logo design, identity design, supervision of implementation.
